key_insight: Halide substitution strongly tunes Ca$_3$PX$_3$ perovskites, with iodine-rich Ca$_3$PI$_3$ emerging as the most stable and photovoltaic-promising composition.
engineering_relevance: These results guide composition engineering of lead-free perovskite-like absorbers toward higher-efficiency solar cells and other optoelectronic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Band structure and optical-parameter analysis across X = F, Cl, Br, I
SLME-based photovoltaic screening for efficiency comparison
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV across the series and SLME up to 29.6% for Ca$_3$PI$_3$, versus 0.6% for Ca$_3$PF$_3$.
watch_item: The very high efficiency is a theoretical screening result, so experimental validation and stability under real device conditions are still needed.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
